summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of septic arthritis of the left shoulder, aortic stenosis, and SIADH was admitted from rehab with erythema of the left shoulder and found to have strep viridans bacteremia. Though the left shoulder was not reinfected, fluid from the right shoulder showed elevated white blood cells, indicating early septic arthritis. He was treated with ceftriaxone after switching from clindamycin, and a new PICC line was placed for antibiotic administration. His shoulder erythema was determined to be non-infectious, likely post-surgical. Hyponatremia improved with fluid restriction, and warfarin was held ahead of a planned spinal injection. He remained stable, with improving inflammatory markers, and was discharged to extended care for completion of antibiotics, follow-up with infectious disease and orthopedics, and resumption of anticoagulation after the procedure.
problems: Streptococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, other streptococcus
Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, shoulder region
